report.summary: Alert EVAL-02 on host WS-FIN-11 indicates an active compromise involving rundll32.exe executing a DLL from a user-writable profile directory, performing discovery commands, and establishing periodic HTTPS beaconing to an external IP matching past true-positive alerts.

claims.text: Alert EVAL-02 reported periodic outbound HTTPS from rundll32.exe on host WS-FIN-11.
Host WS-FIN-11 generated 5 process events, 20 network connections, and 1 DNS query during the incident window.
rundll32.exe (PID 6120) loaded a DLL from a user-writable path via command line 'rundll32.exe C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Crypto\upd.dll,Start'.
cmd.exe executed three discovery commands (whoami, net group, nltest trusts) spawned via rundll32.exe.
rundll32.exe made 20 outbound HTTPS connections to external IP 198.51.100.23 (cdn-sync.badupdate.example).
Network traffic exhibited likely beaconing behavior every ~60.2 seconds with low interval and byte variation.
No DNS anomalies were observed in the single query performed.
The domain cdn-sync.badupdate.example and IP 198.51.100.23 matched past true-positive alert PA-2026-0901 involving rundll32 DLL loading and 60-second HTTPS beaconing.

recommended_next_steps: Isolate host WS-FIN-11 from the network immediately to prevent further C2 communication and potential lateral movement.
Collect a full forensic artifact package from WS-FIN-11, including memory and the suspicious file C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Crypto\upd.dll.
Block external IP 198.51.100.23 and domain cdn-sync.badupdate.example across perimeter firewalls and web proxies.
Hunt across the enterprise for process executions of rundll32.exe loading DLLs from user AppData directories and similar C2 traffic profiles.
Tune EDR detection rules to alert on rundll32.exe executing payloads from non-standard user profile paths.
